name: Why is my water pressure suddenly low in one faucet but not others?

mainEntity.name: Why is my water pressure suddenly low in one faucet but not others?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low water pressure in a single faucet often indicates a localized issue rather than a system-wide problem. Common causes include a clogged aerator, a faulty cartridge in the faucet, or an obstruction in the supply line to that specific fixture. Checking and cleaning the aerator is a good first step, as mineral deposits can easily build up and restrict flow. If the problem persists, it may require a plumber to diagnose and repair the internal faucet components or clear a blockage in the branch line. A decision factor here is determining if only one fixture is affected, which points to a localized fix rather than a more extensive plumbing issue.
